result:
Numbers checked, ready.

**1. SURFACE**
File look standard Prusa Marlin gcode, metric (no G20 seen), absolute XY, right-hand axis (X right, Y "back", Z up), object metadata via M486 (exclude-object feature) with plain-English labels "Embossed text" / "Shape-Box", bbox via M555, firmware check M115/M862 for MK4S. Object S0 label say literal "Embossed text" — surface reading: answer to "what text show" = that string.

**2. CONTENT**
Test mm hypothesis: X max 241mm, Y max 206.574mm fit MK4S bed (250×210mm) fine. Inch hypothesis falsified — 241in→6121mm, 206.574in→5247mm, way over any bed. So mm confirmed, no unit mismatch.
Real mismatch elsewhere: M486 `A` field is PrusaSlicer's *object name* (usually derived from STL filename), not a content field guaranteed to equal glyphs actually toolpathed. Nothing in mechanical data confirms geometry spells "Embossed text" — only X/Y toolpath shape would confirm, and this summary can't render that. Also checked M555 bbox (X 25.079–224.934, Y 2.994–206.849) against G1 extremes: Y max 206.574 fits (margin 0.275mm), but X max 241 exceeds bbox by 16.07mm — some G1 X/Y points lie outside declared object bbox (skirt/purge/wipe-tower, not object geometry). So raw coordinate extremes ≠ pure "text" or "box" geometry.
CONTENT VERDICT: MISMATCH

**3. MISREADINGS**

- **"Object label = printed text content."** Survives as plausible guess, NOT evidence. M486 `A` string is slicer object name metadata, commonly auto-set from filename, can be renamed by user to anything. Must determine actual glyphs by rendering/plotting X/Y toolpath of S0 block (41777 G1-with-E lines), not by reading label string.

- **"Y-axis in gcode reads like image row index (Y down = up)."** Falsified by convention: gcode Y increase = "away from operator" = up in top-down view. Image/pixel coords flip Y. Processor plotting X,Y directly as (col,row) without inverting Y will mirror text vertically. Must render with Y increasing upward (or explicitly flip only if plotting library defaults to row-down).

- **"E values are absolute like X/Y."** Not resolved by given head/summary — no M82/M83 seen in shown HEAD lines, but 234× G92 (likely G92 E0 resets) plus repeating E.7/E-.7 retract pattern hints relative-style bookkeping either way. Must grep full file for M82 (absolute) or M83 (relative extrusion) before trusting any E delta math; wrong assumption breaks flow-based letter-stroke-width inference.

- **"All G1 X/Y extremes (241, -4) belong to the two named objects."** Computed: object bbox from M555 = X[25.079,224.934], Y[2.994,206.849]. X max 241 sits 16.07mm outside that box; Y min -4 also outside Y lower bound 2.994. These out-of-bbox points are non-object toolpath (purge line/wipe tower/skirt), not part of "Embossed text" or "Shape-Box" geometry. Must filter G1 lines to those between `M486 S0`/`M486 S1` and their `M486 S-1` terminators, further bounded within M555 bbox, before reconstructing letterforms — else purge-line moves contaminate the shape.

- **"Z range 0.2–87.88mm means text is engraved/embossed across whole height."** World-knowledge check: 87.88mm is overall multi-object print height (includes Shape-Box object too, whole G1 set). Within S0 (text) block alone, summary states Z min 0.2 max 64.88 — must use per-object Z range, not whole-file Z range, or infer wrong emboss depth/height for text specifically.

- **Dialect check**: command mix (M204 P/R/T split accel, M205 jerk-style, M862.x version-guard, M486 exclude-object) matches PrusaSlicer/Marlin-Prusa firmware convention, not generic RepRap/Klipper dialect — no mismatch there, ruled out as risk.
